Rashi on Menachot 6a:10:1.hebrew: הצד השוה כו' - ולמה לי קרא:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:10:1.english: The common element, etc. - Then why do I need the verse?

Rashi on Menachot 6a:12:1.hebrew: מליקה - טריפה היא לכתחילה, דחותך שדרה ומפרקת, כדאמרי' בפ"ק דשחיטת חולין (דף כ:), והותרה לגבוה מכלל איסורה. להדיוט אישתרי? אף אני אביא טריפה (ולמה לי קרא):
Rashi on Menachot 6a:12:1.english: Pinching - It is a *tereifa* from the outset, since [the one performing it] cuts [the bird's] spine and neck, as we say in the first chapter of [Tractate] Chullin, on the slaughtering [of animals] (page 20b); and it was permitted for the Most High from the general category of its prohibition. [But was it] permitted for a layman? [If so,] I too may bring a *tereifa* (and why do I need a verse?).

Rashi on Menachot 6a:13:1.hebrew: מליקה דחטאת העוף לכהנים - ובבעל מום ויוצא דופן לא אשכחן היתר לכהנים מכלל איסור, דאין בהן שום איסור לגבי כהנים:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:13:1.english: Pinching of a bird sin offering [renders it permitted] to the priests - But in the case of a blemished [animal] and one born by caesarean section, we do not find a permission for the priests [that comes] from the category of a prohibition, since there is no prohibition at all in them with regard to the priests.

Rashi on Menachot 6a:13:2.hebrew: משולחן גבוה הוא דזכו - וגבי גבוה אשכחן בבעל מום בעופות היתר מכלל איסור, וליכא מה להצד השוה כו', ול"ל קרא:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:13:2.english: It is from the table of the Most High that they receive - And with regard to the Most High [i.e., the altar], we find in the case of a blemished bird a permission arising out of a general prohibition, and there is no [room for the objection] "what [is true] of the [shared] aspect," etc. And why do I need a verse?

Rashi on Menachot 6a:14:1.hebrew: בעל מום מומן ניכר - שאין מומן פסול אלא בגלוי, כדאמרינן בבכורות בפ' על אלו מומין (בכורות דף לז.). ויוצא דופן מומו ניכר, דאית ליה קלא והכל יודעים:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:14:1.english: A blemished animal, whose blemish is noticeable - For their blemish disqualifies only when it is visible, as we say in Bekhorot, in the chapter [entitled] "Al Elu Mumin" (Bekhorot 37a). And an animal born by caesarean section, its blemish is noticeable, for it has a public reputation and everyone knows [of it].

Rashi on Menachot 6a:14:2.hebrew: טריפה יש שאין מומם ניכר - כגון בבני מעיים:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:14:2.english: A tereifa — there are [cases] where their blemish is not noticeable - For example, in the intestines.

Rashi on Menachot 6a:17:1.hebrew: שלא היתה לה שעת הכושר - דנטרפה ממעי אמה, דומיא דערלה וכלאי הכרם, דכתיב בההוא קרא דכתיב ביה "מן הצאן, מן המאתים, ממשקה ישראל". ואמרינן בפרק אלו עוברין במסכת פסחים (דף מח.): "מן המאתים" — מן המותר ב' מאות שנשתיירו בבור, מכאן לערלה שבטלה במאתים:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:17:1.english: That it did not have a period of fitness - [Meaning,] that it became a tereifa in its mother's womb, similar to orla and diverse kinds in a vineyard, as it is written in that same verse in which it is written, "from the flock, from the two hundred, from the well-watered pastures of Israel." And we said in the chapter Eilu Overin in tractate Pesachim (48a): "From the two hundred" — from the permitted [wine], [if] two hundred [measures] remained in a pit; from here [we learn] that orla is nullified in two hundred [parts].

Rashi on Menachot 6a:19:1.hebrew: זר ואונן - וכל הני מפרש בזבחים (דף טו:) מקראי, דעבודתן פסולה, ואזהרתן בסנהדרין בסוף אלו הן הנשרפין (דף פג.):
Rashi on Menachot 6a:19:1.english: A non-priest and an acute mourner - And all of these [cases] are explained in Zevachim (15b) from verses [showing] that their service is invalid; and the warning against [their performing the service] is in Sanhedrin, at the end of [the chapter] "These are the ones who are burned" (83a):

Rashi on Menachot 6a:19:2.hebrew: ערל - כהן ערל, דהיינו שמתו אחיו מחמת מילה:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:19:2.english: An uncircumcised [priest] - A priest who is uncircumcised, [that is, one] whose brothers died as a result of circumcision.

Rashi on Menachot 6a:19:3.english: Sitting - [For] it is written, "to stand to serve" (Deuteronomy 18:5).

Rashi on Menachot 6a:19:4.hebrew: ע"ג כלים או ע"ג בהמה או רגל חבירו - הגמרא בזבחים (דף כד.) מפרש דבעינן שלא יהא דבר חוצץ בין רגליו לבין הרצפה:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:19:4.english: Upon vessels, or upon an animal, or upon the foot of his fellow - [The Gemara] in Zevachim (24a) explains that we require that nothing intervene between his feet and the floor.

Rashi on Menachot 6a:1:1.hebrew: מצותו בכך - גזירת הכתוב שלא יהא אבנט אלא של כלאים, דכתיב (שמות כח) תכלת וארגמן וגו'. ואמרינן יבמות (דף ד:): מדשש כיתנא, תכלת עמרא:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:1:1.english: Its mitzva is in this [manner] - It is a decree of the verse that the belt may be made only of diverse kinds, as it is written (Exodus 28): "blue, and purple, etc." And we say in [tractate] Yevamot (4b): Since [the verse mentions] fine linen [shesh], [it is] linen; [and since it mentions] blue [techelet], [it is] wool.

Rashi on Menachot 6a:20:1.english: Left - The Gemara explains: From where do we derive that [a handful taken with the left hand] is unfit?

Rashi on Menachot 6a:20:2.hebrew: בן בתירה - אכולהו פליג אזר ואונן וכל הנך:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:20:2.english: Ben Beteira - He disagrees with all of them — the [case of a] zar [non-priest], an onen [a priest in the first day of mourning], and all those [other disqualified cases].

Rashi on Menachot 6a:21:1.hebrew: עלה בידו צרור - נמצא קומץ חסר כשיעור מקום הצרור. וכן מלח או לבונה:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:21:1.english: A stone emerged in his hand - The handful is found to be lacking [by] the space [taken up by] the stone. And the same applies to salt or frankincense.

Rashi on Menachot 6a:21:2.hebrew: מבורץ - גדוש. ל"א, שנראה קמח חוצץ בין ראשי אצבעותיו לפס ידו:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:21:2.english: Mevoratz - Heaped. Another explanation: [it is called this] because flour is seen separating [ḥotzetz] between the tips of his fingers and the palm of his hand.

Rashi on Menachot 6a:21:3.hebrew: בראשי אצבעותיו - מעט, שלא פשטו על פס כל היד:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:21:3.english: With the tips of his fingers - [Meaning,] a small amount, [because] he did not spread [his fingers] over the palm of the whole hand.

Rashi on Menachot 6a:23:1.english: So that his offering will not be of superior quality - So that the meal offering will not be attractive.

Rashi on Menachot 6a:23:2.hebrew: חטאת חלב - (היינו חלב) היינו סתם חטאת. חטאת אינה טעונה נסכים בפרק שתי מדות (לקמן מנחות דף צ:):
Rashi on Menachot 6a:23:2.english: The sin offering of [forbidden] fat - (that is, the fat) this is [the same as] an ordinary sin offering. A sin offering does not require libations, [as stated] in the chapter [entitled] Shetei Midot (below, Menachot 90b).

Rashi on Menachot 6a:2:1.hebrew: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי אמר - להכי איצטריך קרא, משום דאיכא למימר: ניהדר דינא ונייתי במה הצד, ונאמר דטריפה מותרת לגבוה:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:2:1.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, said - For this reason the verse was needed: because it is possible to say, let us return to the [a fortiori] argument and derive it by [the method of] "what is the common element," [and conclude] that a *tereifa* is permitted for the Most High [as an offering].

Rashi on Menachot 6a:6:1.hebrew: מקריבין כקריבין - דמום פסול בכהן כמו בזבח. אבל טריפות לא פסיל בכהנים, דתנן בבכורות בפרק מומין אלו (בכורות דף מה:): ואלו כשרין באדם ופסולין בבהמה: אותו ואת בנו, וטריפה, ויוצא דופן. להכי איצטריך קרא:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:6:1.english: Those who sacrifice [are] like those that are sacrificed - For a blemish disqualifies a priest just as it disqualifies a sacrificial animal. But a *tereifa* (an animal or person with a fatal defect) does not disqualify priests, as we learned in Bekhorot, in the chapter [beginning] "These blemishes" (Bekhorot 45b): "And these are valid in a person but invalid in an animal: [an animal] it and its offspring [slaughtered on the same day], a *tereifa*, and one born by caesarean section." Therefore the verse is necessary.

Rashi on Menachot 6a:7:1.hebrew: אמר ליה רב אחא [סבא] לרב אשי - ואכתי ל"ל קרא? הא איכא למימר:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:7:1.english: Rav Aḥa [Sava] said to Rav Ashi - But still, why do I need a verse? Surely there is [something] to say [in rebuttal]:

Rashi on Menachot 6a:7:2.hebrew: יוצא דופן יוכיח - שכהן יוצא דופן כשר לעבודה, וקרבן יוצא דופן פסול, דאמרינן בת"כ: "כי יולד" — פרט ליוצא דופן:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:7:2.english: One born by caesarean section proves [it] - For a priest born by caesarean section is fit for the service, whereas an offering born by caesarean section is unfit, as we say in the Torat Kohanim: "When [it] is born" — this excludes one born by caesarean section.

Rashi on Menachot 6a:8:1.hebrew: מה ליוצא דופן שאינו קדוש בבכורה - דפטר רחם כתיב (שמות יג). תאמר בטריפה שקדושה בבכורה, אם נולד עם טריפתו? הלכך איצטריך קרא:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:8:1.english: What [is notable] about a [animal] born by caesarean section, that it is not sanctified with firstborn status - For it is written "the opener of the womb" (Exodus 13). Would you say [this about] a tereifa, which is sanctified with firstborn status, if it was born with its tereifa [condition]? Therefore, the verse was necessary:

Rashi on Menachot 6a:9:1.hebrew: בעל מום יוכיח - שקדש בבכורה, ואסור לגבוה, ומותר להדיוט. אף אני אביא טריפה, ולמה לי קרא:
Rashi on Menachot 6a:9:1.english: A blemished animal proves - For it is sanctified with the sanctity of a firstborn and is prohibited to the Most High, [and permitted to a layman]. I too will bring [the case of] a *tereifa*, and why do I need a verse?

Tosafot on Menachot 6a:12:1.hebrew: בעל מום נמי הותר בעופות - ונ"ל דהשתא מצי למילף ממחוסר אבר ויוצא דופן. ולבסוף, כשאמר "שכן מומן ניכר", אתי הכל שפיר:
Tosafot on Menachot 6a:12:1.english: A blemished [animal] was also permitted with birds - And it seems to me that now [the Gemara] could derive [the law] from [an animal] lacking a limb and from one born through the side [by caesarean section]. And at the end, when it said, "for their blemish is visible," everything fits well:

Tosafot on Menachot 6a:14:1.hebrew: שכן מומן ניכר - ואין לומר דמחוסר זמן ואותו ואת בנו ומוקצה ונעבד ורובע ואתנן ומחיר יוכיחו, דכל הני יש להם קול יותר מטריפה בבני מעיים שאין יודע כלל; כי היכי דחשיב יוצא דופן מומו ניכר, משום דיש לו קול. ומחיה, דשריא להדיוט ואסורה לגבוה, אין ללמוד טריפה; דמה לחיה, שכן אין במינה לגבוה, ושכן מומה ניכר:
Tosafot on Menachot 6a:14:1.english: Since their blemish is noticeable - And one cannot say that [an animal] lacking the required age, "it and its offspring," a set-aside [animal], an animal that was worshipped, one that mated with a human [i.e., bestiality], a harlot's payment, and the price of a dog will prove [the inference]; for all of these have publicity [i.e., they are publicly known] more than a *tereifa* with [a defect in] the intestines, which one does not know at all. Just as a [animal born by] caesarean section is considered to have a noticeable blemish, because it has publicity. And as for a wild animal (*chayah*), which is permitted to a layman but forbidden to the Most High [i.e., the altar], one cannot learn [the law of] a *tereifa* from it; for what [is true] of a *chayah*, [is that] its species has nothing [fit] for the altar, and that its blemish is noticeable.

Tosafot on Menachot 6a:17:1.hebrew: דומיא דערלה וכלאי הכרם - וא"ת: והא אמרינן פ' כל שעה (פסחים דף כה.) ובכל הבשר (חולין דף קטז.): זאת אומרת, כלאי הכרם עיקרן נאסר, הואיל והיתה להם שעת הכושר קודם השרשה. ויש לומר, דכלאים דכתיבי בהאי קרא איירי בענבים שעושין מהם יין לנסכים, כדדרשינן (פסחים דף מח.) "מן המאתים" — ממותר ב' מאות שנשתיירו בבור, הנהו לא היתה להם שעת הכושר. דדוקא דחרצן שנזרע הוא שהיתה לו שעת הכושר קודם השרשה, ומן החרצן אין עושין נסכים. וא"ת: אותם ענבים עצמן היתה להם שעת הכושר קודם שהוסיפו מאתים? וי"ל דמה שנתוסף באיסור אחר שנעשה כלאים, שגדל אחרי כן, לא היה לו מעולם (אחרי כן) שעת הכושר. והאי דמיתסר אף מה שגדל קודם לכן, לפי שא"א להבדיל זה מזה להפריש תערובתם:
Tosafot on Menachot 6a:17:1.english: Similar to orla and diverse kinds in a vineyard - And if you ask: But didn't we say in the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 25a) and in [the chapter] Kol HaBasar (Chullin 116a): This means that diverse kinds of the vineyard were prohibited from their very origin, since they had a period of fitness before taking root? And one can answer that the diverse kinds written in this verse speak of grapes from which wine is made for libations, as we expound (Pesachim 48a): "From the two hundred" — from the surplus of the two hundred [grapes] that remained in the pit; those did not have a period of fitness. For it is only the grape seed that was sown that had a period of fitness before taking root, and from the seed one does not make libations. And if you ask: Those very grapes themselves had a period of fitness before the two hundred were added? One can answer that what was added in a prohibited state, after it became diverse kinds, [and] that grew afterwards, never had (afterwards) a period of fitness. And the fact that even what grew before that became prohibited is because it is impossible to separate one from the other, to set apart their mixture:

Tosafot on Menachot 6a:17:2.hebrew: כתב רחמנא כל אשר יעבור - אע"ג דמוכח דהיכא שהיתה לו שעת הכושר לא ילפינן ממשקה ישראל, אפ"ה מייתי ליה בכל דוכתא בפ' כל האסורין (תמורה דף כט.) גבי נעבד, משום דע"י תלתא קראי מסקינן דאין לחלק:
Tosafot on Menachot 6a:17:2.english: The Merciful One wrote, "Whatever passes [under the rod]" - Even though it is evident that in a case where [the animal] had a period of fitness, we do not derive [its disqualification] from "the well-watered pastures of Israel," nevertheless [the Gemara] cites it everywhere, in the chapter [entitled] Kol Ha'asurin (Temurah 29a), with regard to an animal that was worshipped, because through three verses we conclude that one does not distinguish [between the cases]:

Tosafot on Menachot 6a:19:1.hebrew: שקמצן זר אונן כו' - והוא הדין ששתויי יין ופרועי ראש פסולים, והם במיתה, ומחלי עבודה, כדאמרינן בפרק אלו הן הנשרפין (סנהדרין דף פג:), ותנא ושייר:
Tosafot on Menachot 6a:19:1.english: "Whose handful was removed by a non-priest, an acute mourner, etc." - The same law applies to those who are drunk with wine and those with unkempt hair [who performed the service] — [they are liable to] death, and they profane the service, as we say in the chapter "Elu Hen HaNisrafin" (Sanhedrin 83b); and the Tanna [of our Mishnah] listed [some cases] and left others out.

Tosafot on Menachot 6a:1:1.hebrew: מה לכלאים שכן מצותו בכך - ואע"ג דאפשר לקיים בטלית של צמר, מ"מ בסדין של פשתן שחייב בציצית לא אפשר לקיים בכך. וא"ת: ולימא גיד הנשה במחובר יוכיח, דאין מצותו בכך, ושרי לגבוה, כדאמר בריש ג"ה (חולין צ:): וכי תימא מה לג"ה שכן מחובר, הנך יוכיחו. וי"ל: כיון דאין לו היתר אלא על ידי חיבור, לא שייך למיעבד מיניה יוכיח:
Tosafot on Menachot 6a:1:1.english: "What is notable about diverse kinds, that its mitzvah is in this [manner]?" - Even though it is possible to fulfill [the mitzvah of tzitzit] with a woolen garment, nevertheless with a linen sheet, which is obligated in tzitzit, it is not possible to fulfill [the mitzvah] in this [manner]. And if you ask: But let us say that the sciatic nerve, [when it is] attached, will prove [the point], for its mitzvah is not in this [manner], and it is permitted for the Most High [as an offering], as it says at the beginning of [the chapter on] the sciatic nerve (Chullin 90b): "And if you say, what is notable about the sciatic nerve, that it is attached — these [other cases] will prove it." And one can answer: Since it has no permissibility except through [its] attachment, it is not applicable to derive a "will prove" argument from it:

Tosafot on Menachot 6a:20:1.hebrew: בן בתירא אומר יחזור ויקמוץ בימין - למאי דמוכח בגמרא דהוא הדין אכולהו פסולי דלעיל, יש לתמוה דלא עריב פסול שמאל בהדי פסולי דלעיל. וי"ל משום דס"ד דשמאל, כיון דאית ליה הכשירא ביום הכיפורים, קבוע עבודה, ולא תועיל בה חזרה:
Tosafot on Menachot 6a:20:1.english: Ben Beteira says: He must return and remove the handful again with the right hand - According to what is demonstrated in the Gemara, that the same applies to all the disqualifications mentioned above, it is puzzling [why the Mishnah] did not combine the disqualification of the left hand together with the disqualifications above. And one can answer: Because one might have thought that [regarding] the left hand, since it has a [case of] validity on Yom Kippur, the service is fixed [as performed], and returning would not help it.

Tosafot on Menachot 6a:21:1.hebrew: חסר שקמצו בראשי אצבעותיו - אגב דמפרש יתר, חוזר ומפרש חסר כיוצא בו, אף על גב דצרור וגרגיר וקורט משום חסר הוא:
Tosafot on Menachot 6a:21:1.english: "Lacking" is where he removed the handful with the tips of his fingers - Since [the Mishnah] explains "outsized," it goes on to explain "lacking" in a similar manner, even though [the case of] a stone, a grain [of salt], or a pinch [of frankincense] is [also unfit] because of [the category of] "lacking."
